questions.question: When doing a parallel parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it slowly. Move your vehicle's rear as close as possible to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: If students cause a disturbance on the bus while others are getting off, what should you do?

options.text: Walk to the back right away and handle the disturbance while students unload.
Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the disturbance.
Have another student handle it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the disturbance.
questions.explanation: You need your full attention when loading or unloading students. If a behavior problem happens, wait until all students are safely off the bus before you deal with it.

questions.question: When should you adjust a bus's mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving the bus.
While you are driving the bus.
At the first traffic light after you start your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving the bus.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start any trip.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Only once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This routine helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: What should happen when students load and unload a bus?

options.text: It is simple and does not need supervision.
It is dangerous and must be supervised.
It can happen without the driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is dangerous and must be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow safety rules during these times. Loading and unloading must always be supervised.

questions.question: What is true about loading and unloading a bus?

options.text: It can be dangerous for passengers.
It does not need supervision.
It should be done while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow safety rules during these times.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS stops working, what happens?

options.text: You will lose all brakes.
You will still have brakes.
You should use only the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) keep wheels from locking when you brake hard. If ABS breaks, your regular brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Why should you park at least 10 feet away from students when picking them up?

options.text: You can see all their movements clearly.
It will be hard to park closer.
Students need exercise from walking.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see all their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Park your bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students. This is safest because students must walk to the bus, and you can watch them the whole time.

questions.question: What can you NOT see with properly adjusted crossover mirrors?

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors let you see in front of the bus from the bumper to where you have direct vision. You can also see the right and left front tires touching the ground and the area from the front to the service door. You cannot see the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks while driving a school bus, what should you do?

options.text: Check the tracks but keep driving without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Stop at every railroad crossing. Park between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail so you can see the tracks clearly. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: In general, how is student safety best maintained?

options.text: Keep students on the bus.
Let some students leave the bus.
Let students leave the bus and spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest when they stay on the school bus. It is easier to keep them under control. Students should stay on the bus unless staying puts them in danger.

questions.question: Bus doors should stay closed while driving. When is the one exception?

options.text: When crossing railroad tracks.
When you need to cool down the bus.
When there is no other vehicle next to the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Bus doors must stay closed while the bus is moving. The only exception is when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what might happen?

options.text: You will not need to do anything related to railroad crossings.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: During your driving test, if the route does not have a real railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the proper steps at a practice location.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Keep one hand on the handrail.
Exit quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep one hand on the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting the bus, face the bus and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in an automatic test failure.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: While driving.
Before you start driving.
After you finish driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: It is very important to adjust all mirrors correctly before operating the bus. Always check each mirror before you start driving.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Stay in control on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control on slippery surfaces.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent the brakes from locking up on slippery surfaces. ABS helps you keep control if you brake hard on a slippery road. Drive and brake the same way in a vehicle with or without ABS.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go back up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not try to drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Before picking up students, what must a driver ensure?

options.text: All nearby traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling students to come.
The red lights are turned on.
The bus is pulled to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All nearby traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling students to come.
questions.explanation: Before opening the bus door to pick up students, make sure all nearby traffic has come to a complete stop. Then signal the students to approach.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, how many points of contact must you maintain?

options.text: Three points of contact
Four points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: When exiting the vehicle, face it and always keep three points of contact. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in an automatic test failure.

questions.question: If a student may have a back injury, what should you do?

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Do not move them.
Ask them to try to stand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them.
questions.explanation: Do not move a student who may have a neck or back injury unless their life is in immediate danger.
